agente-devops.name: agente-devops
agente-devops.description: Use to audit, generate, and manage secure Docker container configurations (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml) and DevOps CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions). Aligned with SCM, IEEE 730, and ISO 27001 standards.

agente-ideas.name: agente-ideas
agente-ideas.description: Agente experto en deliberación y consenso. Resuelve decisiones altamente complejas o ambiguas ejecutando un consejo de 3 etapas (propuestas en paralelo, revisión anónima cruzada y síntesis final).

audit-loop.name: audit-loop
audit-loop.description: Orchestrates the closed loop: audit → fix → re-audit → iterate. Activated as a follow-up of audits (security, marketing, finops).

auditor-de-marketing.name: auditor-de-marketing
auditor-de-marketing.description: Use to audit website growth, on-page SEO, schema markup, AI search optimization (AEO/GEO), programmatic SEO, social sharing cards (OpenGraph), readability, copy quality, AI writing detection (30 patterns), CRO, and CTA conversion.

auditor-de-seguridad.name: auditor-de-seguridad
auditor-de-seguridad.description: Use when completing development, before deployment, after vibecoding/AI code generation, or when reviewing project security. Covers secrets, dependencies, SAST (OWASP Top 10), rate limiting, authentication, session management, API security, encryption, logging, compliance, infrastructure, database, and CI/CD.

brainstorming.name: brainstorming
brainstorming.description: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.

changelog-generator.name: changelog-generator
changelog-generator.description: Genera notas de lanzamiento (Changelogs) automatizadas y legibles para el usuario final analizando el historial de Git (commits). Clasifica los cambios en categorías lógicas y actualiza el archivo CHANGELOG.md.

code-simplification.name: code-simplification
code-simplification.description: Simplifies code for clarity. Use when refactoring code for clarity without changing behavior. Use when code works but is harder to read, maintain, or extend than it should be. Use when reviewing code that has accumulated unnecessary complexity.

context-engineering.name: context-engineering
context-engineering.description: Optimizes agent context setup. Use when starting a new session, when agent output quality degrades, when switching between tasks, or when you need to configure rules files and context for a project.

creativo-visual.name: creativo-visual
creativo-visual.description: Visual Creative Director for AI image generation and optimization. Translates basic prompts into high-quality technical and artistic specifications, generates web assets (favicons, app icons, social images), manages brand presets, aspect ratios, validates asset quality, and integrates with detected frameworks.

db-schema-detector.name: db-schema-detector
db-schema-detector.description: Detects local databases and generates cached schemas in CodeGraph to save tokens and audit design inconsistencies, security issues, and environment drift between local and production.

dispatching-parallel-agents.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
dispatching-parallel-agents.description: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies

emil-kowalski-design.name: emil-kowalski-design
emil-kowalski-design.description: Use when building, reviewing, or auditing any UI component to apply Emil Kowalski's design engineering principles. Enforces animation quality, micro-interaction polish, perceived performance, and accessibility standards.

executing-plans.name: executing-plans
executing-plans.description: Use when you have a written implementation plan to execute in a separate session with review checkpoints

finishing-a-development-branch.name: finishing-a-development-branch
finishing-a-development-branch.description: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work - guides completion of development work by presenting structured options for merge, PR, or cleanup

gestor-documental.name: gestor-documental
gestor-documental.description: Use to design, audit, format, and validate technical and scientific documents according to APA (7th Edition) and software engineering requirements/testing standards (ISO 29148, ISO 29119).

impeccable-design-taste.name: impeccable-design-taste
impeccable-design-taste.description: Use for any frontend design work, UI generation, or design review where quality must be premium. Activates comprehensive design auditing across typography, color, spacing, motion, and accessibility.

incremental-implementation.name: incremental-implementation
incremental-implementation.description: Delivers changes incrementally. Use when implementing any feature or change that touches more than one file. Use when you're about to write a large amount of code at once, or when a task feels too big to land in one step.

optimizador-finops.name: optimizador-finops
optimizador-finops.description: Use to audit computational resource utilization, API efficiency, and token usage economy. Aligned with SQA & ISO 31000 risk management standards.

playwright-testing.name: playwright-testing
playwright-testing.description: Use when designing, writing, debugging, or auditing Playwright E2E and component tests.

project-manager.name: project-manager
project-manager.description: Project Manager agent. CEO gives high-level direction; Project Manager plans, delegates, reviews, and reports.

receiving-code-review.name: receiving-code-review
receiving-code-review.description: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation

requesting-code-review.name: requesting-code-review
requesting-code-review.description: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements

spec-driven-development.name: spec-driven-development
spec-driven-development.description: Creates specs before coding. Use when starting a new project, feature, or significant change and no specification exists yet. Use when requirements are unclear, ambiguous, or only exist as a vague idea.

subagent-driven-development.name: subagent-driven-development
subagent-driven-development.description: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session

systematic-debugging.name: systematic-debugging
systematic-debugging.description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes

test-driven-development.name: test-driven-development
test-driven-development.description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code

using-git-worktrees.name: using-git-worktrees
using-git-worktrees.description: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback

verification-before-completion.name: verification-before-completion
verification-before-completion.description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always

writing-plans.name: writing-plans
writing-plans.description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code

writing-skills.name: writing-skills
writing-skills.description: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment
